external_entities.name: Shoppers
external_entities.description: Customers who browse the storefront, sign in, and place orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API.
external_entities.notes: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment-status webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: The internet-exposed API through which shoppers browse and place orders, and to which the card processor posts payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run. It is the only thing we expose to the internet.
processes.notes: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that processes orders, reads and writes order data, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network; it is not exposed outside.
processes.notes: The worker uses an application-account password supplied through an environment variable. Its gRPC call from the storefront API has no authentication.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)
data_stores.notes: The order service accesses it with a single application account that has full read/write.

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_stores.notes: Each receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it.

data_flows.name: browse and place orders
data_flows.description: Shoppers browse the storefront and submit orders through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: order submission
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: order data access
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values in orders-db.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.notes: The application-account password comes from an environment variable on the worker.
data_flows.authentication: single application account with password from an environment variable

data_flows.name: receipt write
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.data_description: Receipt recording which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: payment webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor posts a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source states: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone from which shoppers reach the storefront.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: Cloud Run
trust_boundaries.description: The hosting zone for the storefront API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: a Node service running on Cloud Run

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The internal network containing the order service and associated order data.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: Cloud Storage
trust_boundaries.description: The hosting zone for the receipt archive bucket.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API is assigned to the Cloud Run hosting zone.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the storefront API is a Node service running on Cloud Run.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive is assigned to the Cloud Storage hosting zone.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies the receipt archive as a Cloud Storage bucket.

assumptions.assumption: orders-db is in the core network zone with the order service.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly places the order service in the core network and describes that service as the component reading and writing orders-db; it does not separately state the database's network location.
The database contains shopper addresses and card-last-four values, which are personal and payment-related data.
